status_summary: The fleet has not grown toward 355: CRS counted 293 battle force ships on 2025-10-01, and the Navy's Fiscal Year 2027 shipbuilding plan (released 2026-05-10; excerpt reprinted by USNI News) puts it at 291 against 355 required by law, a goal CRS traces to the FY2018 NDAA. The release pairs the plan with a 65.8 billion dollar FY2027 shipbuilding request and a 30-year Golden Fleet investment plan. The July 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21, Sec. 20002) provides 29,176 million dollars for shipbuilding per CRS, and the FY2026 NDAA (P.L. 119-60) carries sections on medium and large unmanned surface vessels, Modular Attack Surface Craft, amphibious force structure and unmanned vessel technical authority (titles only read). On 2025-12-22 the President announced a Golden Fleet concept with a Trump-class battleship and a new frigate; Breaking Defense reported that the Constellation frigate order was cut from 20 ships to two, and CRS listed planned numbers of 15 to 25 battleships and 50 to 65 frigates in January 2026. CBO estimated the lead battleship at roughly 14.3 to 20.6 billion dollars (per Breaking Defense), and CBO's testimony of 2026-04-22 says the Navy plans 15 to 25 battleships to replace 28 planned DDG(X) destroyers and estimates the fleet will average about 20 ships fewer in 2026 to 2030 than historical build speeds would have produced. The FY2026 request covers 19 new ships, 16 funded through the 2025 reconciliation act. On unmanned systems, the Navy replaced one program with a medium unmanned surface vessel marketplace in March 2026, its plan describes unmanned systems integrated with the crewed force, and it opened a robotics and autonomous systems development center on 2026-09-24. No re-created General Board or Navy Rapid Capabilities Office was found in the plan excerpt, the CRS report or news coverage reviewed, and munitions production rates were not verified.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14269 signed. It orders a Maritime Action Plan, shipbuilding incentives, and a review of government vessel procurement and the maritime industrial base for national security.
P.L. 119-21 is enacted; its Sec. 20002 is titled Enhancement of Department of Defense resources for shipbuilding, and CRS lists 29,176 million dollars enacted for the section (section text not read).

The FY2026 NDAA becomes law as P.L. 119-60; its table of contents lists Sec. 122 (modification to limitations on Navy medium and large unmanned surface vessels), Sec. 130 (limitation on construction of Modular Attack Surface Craft), Sec. 1011 (requirements for amphibious warfare ship force structure) and Sec. 1020 (exemption of unmanned surface vessels and unmanned underwater vehicles from certain technical authority requirements); section text not read.

The President announces the Golden Fleet and a Trump-class battleship program at Mar-a-Lago; reporting says two ships would start quickly, the class could reach 20 to 25, and the Constellation frigate order was cut from 20 to two with a new frigate planned.
CBO estimates the lead battleship at 14.3 to 20.6 billion dollars and follow-on ships at 9 to 13 billion each (January 2026; day not given, first of month used).

CRS reports 293 battle force ships as of 2025-10-01 and a FY2026 request for 19 new ships (16 funded by the 2025 reconciliation act); the Golden Fleet goal was not yet released in detail beyond planned numbers of 15 to 25 battleships and 50 to 65 frigates, and CRS did not mention a General Board or Rapid Capabilities Office.

The Navy ends the MASC unmanned surface vessel program and starts a marketplace for production-ready medium unmanned vessels, with the first production vessel expected in FY2027 (March 2026; day not given, first of month used).

Congressional Budget Office testimony (Eric Labs) to two House subcommittees: the Navy plans to buy 15 to 25 guided missile battleships (35,000 tons or more) that would replace 28 planned DDG(X) destroyers; the fleet has never grown as large as Navy plans envisioned, and from 2026 to 2030 would be about 20 ships smaller on average than historical build speeds would give; the testimony gives no dollar estimate for the battleship program.

The Department of the Navy releases its Fiscal Year 2027 Shipbuilding Plan with a 30-year investment plan for the Golden Fleet and a 65.8 billion dollar FY2027 shipbuilding request. The plan excerpt reprinted by USNI News on 2026-05-11 reports 291 battle force ships against 355 required by law, unmanned systems integrated with the crewed force, and a goal of raising the share of shipbuilding work at distributed sites from about 10 percent to 50 percent; the full plan was not read.

title: Build a Navy of more than 355 ships and field unmanned systems
uncertainties: The USNI page reproduces only the plan's introduction and the CRS report text was read through its first 100,000 characters, so the plan's ship-buy numbers, any General Board or Rapid Capabilities Office, and munitions production were not found; absence in these sources is not confirmed absence. The fleet counts (293 on 2025-10-01, 291 in the May 2026 plan) come from different sources and dates. No primary Navy or White House document for the Golden Fleet announcement was found; details come from Breaking Defense and CRS. Munitions and amphibious-ship items on the same Mandate pages were not researched. The Mandate's 355 figure matches the statutory requirement the Navy cites, but the CRS report describes an older 381-ship goal that the Golden Fleet goal is to replace. Month-only events use first-of-month dates. CBO's testimony of 2026-04-22 was read in full on cbo.gov; it confirms the battleship plan and fleet-size shortfall but gives no battleship cost, so the 14.3 to 20.6 billion dollar figure remains from Breaking Defense's report of a separate CBO estimate (not located on cbo.gov). The CRS report on congress.gov blocks automated fetches, so the CRS figures rest on a mirror (everycrsreport.com). The DocumentCloud copy of the Navy plan returned HTTP 403. No White House or Department of War document for the December 2025 Golden Fleet announcement was found. The plan PDF is on a Department of Defense media host that refuses automated fetches, so the plan was read only through the Navy press release (no ship counts) and the USNI excerpt; the official title is the Fiscal Year 2027 Shipbuilding Plan. A trade article reports a 355-ship crewed target by FY2040, 122 ships (63 uncrewed) and 15 battleships over 30 years; none of these was verified against the plan and none is used for the stage. The body text of P.L. 119-21 Sec. 20002 and of the shipbuilding sections of P.L. 119-60 lies beyond the point where the govinfo.gov pages end, so section titles come from the tables of contents and the Sec. 20002 amount from CRS.
